clue.text: ITV repeat broadcast about union abuse

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the single letter that follows
broadcast in its sense of scattered, as seed is, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
U is an abbreviation for union, as in EU or TUC

explanation.surface: A television channel shows an old programme again, one concerning the mistreatment of trade union members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges ITV REPEAT into VITPERATE, and 'about' wraps that round U. ITV is a British commercial television channel, which makes the surface natural.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to abuse someone in words is to berate or revile them harshly.

clue.text: Food some have a lot

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that certain people own plenty to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: calf meat is one kind of thing to eat.

clue.text: City aware of rent having been reduced at top level

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece at the top level is the one written first
reduced means the word for rent is shortened by losing its last letter

parts.note: rent as a past participle means torn, as in a rent garment
to be onto someone is to be aware of what they are up to

explanation.surface: A town council knows that housing costs have been lowered by a decision of the highest authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been reduced' cuts TORN to TOR, and 'at top level' places it above ONTO in this down entry. 'rent' looks like housing payment but is the old participle of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is the largest metropolis in Canada, on Lake Ontario.

clue.text: What the energy minister has to succeed in?

definitions.text: What the energy minister has to succeed in?

parts.words: What the energy minister has to succeed in?
parts.note: a pun: the statecraft of a minister whose brief is electricity and fuel, read against the phrase for diplomacy backed by threat of force

explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical reading: the phrase really means statecraft backed by strength, here taken as the governmental business of electricity.

clue.text: Furniture craftsman possibly concerned with shop on river

indicators.note: on in a down entry puts what comes before it on top of the piece after it

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as at the head of a letter
a store is a shop
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A cabinet-maker might well take an interest in a retail premises beside the water.
explanation.definitionFit: An example, hence 'possibly': someone who repairs and renovates antique chairs and tables is one kind of such a person.

clue.text: Term for unintelligent bumpkin

indicators.note: term here is an end or limit, so the term for a word is its final letter

parts.note: a hick is a disparaging word for an unsophisticated country person

explanation.surface: A word you might use of a dim yokel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition. 'Term for' takes the closing letter of 'unintelligent', since a term is an end; then a bumpkin follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the word is informal British for stupid or slow-witted, just what one calls a dim yokel.

clue.text: Dull liberal in broadcast

indicators.note: in says the single letter sits inside the word that follows it

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it by scattering
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics

explanation.surface: A boring politician of the centre appears on a radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a dull pupil or a dull evening is one that is sluggish or tedious.

clue.text: One terribly boring fat man

indicators.note: boring in the sense of drilling into, so the rearranged letters go inside the word after

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking

indicators.note: terribly suggests things done badly, so the letters of the word before are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadfully tedious, overweight fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges ONE into EON, and 'boring' drills that into LARD. The surface makes 'boring' an adjective for a tedious man.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a male first name, as borne by Bernstein and Cohen.

clue.text: Articulate writer touring in order to support a cathedral city

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece that supports sits underneath, so the other piece comes first

parts.note: Wells in Somerset is England's smallest cathedral city

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word before it surrounds what follows

parts.note: a pen is a thing that writes
OK means in order, all right

explanation.surface: An eloquent author travels around so as to give backing to a town with a famous church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' wraps the writing implement round the two-letter approval, and 'to support' sets that underneath, since this is a down entry. The city is a small one in Somerset, south-west England, known for its cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an articulate person talks clearly and correctly, with a refined manner.

clue.text: Pointer from 'igh school?

indicators.note: the dropped aitch in 'igh shows a speaker who leaves the opening h off words, so the school loses its first letter

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school, at Harrow on the Hill

explanation.surface: A cockney speaker mentions something that points the way out of secondary education.
explanation.walkthrough: ''igh' is written with its aitch dropped, telling us to drop the H from HARROW, a famous English boys' boarding school standing on a hill, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a sign or cursor with this shape shows direction.

clue.text: Tube? — it's often jam packed

parts.note: the Tube is London's crowded underground railway, but here a tube is a cylinder of sponge cake literally filled with jam

explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: this cake is a sponge sheet spread with fruit preserve and wound into a cylinder.

clue.text: Mortuaries set to develop grave issue

indicators.note: to develop is to change form, so the letters before it grow into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Funeral premises are about to face a problem to do with burial plots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to develop' rearranges the thirteen letters of MORTUARIES SET. 'grave' reads as a burial place beside the mortuaries but means weighty.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym phrase: a grave issue is a weighty affair, not something to joke about.

clue.text: Look for sun and brand new holiday area

indicators.note: new says the letters before it are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
S is an abbreviation for Sun, as in days of the week
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tourist seeks sunshine and a completely fresh place to go on vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges LOOK FOR, S and BRAND together. The answer is a network of rivers and lakes in eastern England, popular for boating holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: these East Anglian waterways are a well-known British boating destination.

clue.text: Crazy paving dreadfully disturbed individual

parts.note: psycho is slang for crazy, as an adjective
a path is a paved way, so paving can stand for it

explanation.surface: Someone badly upset by a patio of irregular broken slabs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy paving' is a British term for a path of irregular broken slabs; here the two words are split and read separately, and 'dreadfully' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a person with a severe personality disorder, lacking conscience and empathy.

clue.text: Break in journey finished after a great deal all round

indicators.note: after says the word for finished follows the other piece
all round turns the word before it right about, so it is read from its end

parts.note: pots, as in pots of money, means a great deal
over means finished, as in the match is over

explanation.surface: A pause on a trip ended once a big bargain had been struck with everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all round' reads the plural word for a great deal from its end, and 'after' sends the word for finished behind it. 'deal' looks like a bargain but is part of a quantity phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a short stay at an intermediate place, especially between flights.

clue.text: Gangster rings, causing bad luck

parts.note: hood is American slang for a gangster, short for hoodlum
the letter O looks like a ring, and rings in the plural gives two of them

explanation.surface: A mobster makes phone calls and misfortune follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a jinx or run of misfortune, as when a team cannot win at one ground.

clue.text: French composer of unusual tameness

indicators.note: unusual says the letters after it are put in an order that is not their normal one

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician from France who is remarkably docile.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Jules of that name wrote the operas Manon and Werther in Paris.

clue.text: With rotters hanging around, daughter and I fly

indicators.note: hanging around says the word for rotters stands on both sides of the other letters

parts.note: cads are rotters, dishonourable men
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: With unpleasant men loitering nearby, a parent and child take a plane out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging around' puts CADS round D and I. 'fly' reads as a verb but is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a moth-like insect whose larvae live in streams, much copied by anglers.

clue.text: One's not realistic about stopping armed criminal

indicators.note: stopping in the sense of plugging, as a stopper does, so the word before it goes inside what follows
criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters of the word before are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Somebody is being naive when it comes to halting a crook with a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges ARMED into DAMER, and 'stopping' plugs RE into it. 'One's' is 'one is', part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: an idealist or fantasist lives in hopes rather than facts.

clue.text: Fantastic Sudanese artiste

indicators.note: fantastic in the sense of strange or fanciful, so the letters after it take a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A marvellous performer from Sudan.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a female ballet performer is one kind of stage entertainer.

clue.text: To some extent founder going for experience

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A company's creator is leaving partly to gain know-how.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for experience' as the definition, but 'for' only joins wordplay to definition: the answer is a verb and swaps with 'experience' alone, as in experience hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to experience an operation or a change is to go through it.

clue.text: Snog and then it's finished? Could be "brief encounter"

indicators.note: finished in the sense of ruined or done for, so the letters before it are broken up

parts.note: taken as written, without the possessive-looking s which stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A kiss and it's all over, rather like the famous film romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finished' rearranges SNOG AND THEN IT; the 's is just 'is'. Snog is British slang for a long kiss, and Brief Encounter is a classic 1945 British film romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a sexual liaison lasting only until morning is a short meeting indeed.

clue.text: Swimming in riyadh out of depth is dangerous

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about loosely, so the letters that follow drift into a new order
out of says the abbreviation after it is missing from the word before

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for depth in measurements

explanation.surface: Bathing in the Saudi capital where you cannot touch the bottom is risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' takes D from RIYADH, leaving RIYAH, and 'Swimming in' rearranges those five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: a scary or risky moment is described this way.

clue.text: No prime co-ops cry over spilt milk?

indicators.note: prime means first, so with no prime the word after loses its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Without top-quality grocery shops, people weep about a dairy accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No prime' removes the first letter C from CO-OPS. The definition plays on the proverb about not crying over spilt milk: this is what you actually exclaim. The Co-op is a British grocery chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical example: it is the exclamation made on a small accident such as knocking a glass over.

clue.text: One day, aim for entry

parts.note: a can mean one, as in a pound each
a mission is an aim or purpose one is set on

explanation.surface: Somebody hopes to be let in eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the right or act of going in, as in a ticket price at the door.

clue.text: Fish with tail cut off found in car

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing loosely for a noun, a thing that is fitted in some cars

indicators.note: the tail is the last letter, so the word for the fish loses its final letter

parts.note: a turbot is a large flatfish

explanation.surface: A trimmed piece of seafood is discovered in a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with tail cut off' drops the last letter of TURBOT. The definition is loose: a part some engines have.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose description: a supercharger driven by exhaust gas is fitted to many engines.

clue.text: Us lyricist's courage mentioned

definitions.note: the possessive s reads as 'is'; the definition is the American songwriter himself

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word for courage is taken by its sound

parts.note: heart means courage, as in to lose heart

explanation.surface: People spoke of the bravery of an American songwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioned' asks for a word that sounds like HEART. Lorenz of that name wrote the words for Richard Rodgers's songs.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Lorenz, partner of Richard Rodgers, wrote the words of Blue Moon and My Funny Valentine.

clue.text: Cryptic item's yours to be solved

indicators.note: solving means working something out, so the letters before it are to be worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A puzzling object is handed to you to work out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be solved' rearranges ITEMS YOURS. The surface sounds like a crossword talking about its own clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something cryptic is puzzling or enigmatic, hard to explain.
